name: Lean one-pager
description: A one-page, assumption-driven PRD for a startup or a new bet where speed of learning matters more than completeness.
promptDelta:
Compress the outline into a one-page lean PRD (about 400 words) instead of the full section list.
- Use only these sections: Problem, Who it's for, Riskiest assumption, Smallest test (the MVP or experiment that tests it), Success signal (a metric and threshold that decides continue / pivot / stop), Non-goals, Open questions.
- Drop user stories and detailed requirements.
- Prefer a measurable learning goal over a feature list.
- Leave any threshold you can't derive from the inputs as `[DATA NEEDED: ...]`.

name: Enterprise with compliance & sign-off
description: Adds stakeholders, compliance, security review, rollout controls and a sign-off table for organizations with formal approval gates.
promptDelta:
Expand the outline for an enterprise setting with formal review. Add these sections:
- **Stakeholders & RACI**: roles, not invented names. Who approves scope, security, legal/privacy and launch.
- **Compliance & Regulatory Considerations**: data classification, privacy, retention, accessibility and audit logging. Name regulations or standards only as "to be confirmed with legal/compliance"; do not assert that they apply.
- **Security Review**: what the security team will need to assess.
- **Non-Functional Requirements**: availability, performance, data residency. Use `[DATA NEEDED: ...]` where targets aren't given.
- **Rollout & Change Management**: pilot group, admin controls, feature flags, migration, training and documentation.
- **Sign-off**: a table (Area | Approver role | Status | Date) with Status set to Pending and Date left blank. Do not invent approvers or dates.

name: Engineering handoff
description: Makes the PRD build-ready: acceptance criteria, numbered requirements, edge cases and analytics events.
promptDelta:
Write the PRD for engineering handoff:
- Give every user story acceptance criteria in Given / When / Then form.
- Number functional requirements (FR-1, FR-2, ...) and link each to the goal it serves.
- List edge cases and error states for each core flow.
- Add an analytics table (Event | Trigger | Properties) that measures the primary KPIs.
- Mark anything engineering should decide as an open design decision, not a requirement.
